scenarios.context: Two friends talk about finding work for the holidays.

speakerA.en: Are you going to look for a summer job this year, Sara?
Have you seen any adverts? The café near the park needs a waiter.
Experience isn't always necessary. Employers often want someone reliable and friendly.
Then you should apply today. Send them your CV and a short message.

speakerB.en: Yes, I want to earn some money. I'm saving up for a laptop.
I saw it. I'm not sure I have enough experience, though.
That's true. I'm good with people, and I can work on weekends.
Good idea. I'll write it tonight and take it there tomorrow.

scenarios.context: A student asks her uncle for advice before an interview.

speakerA.en: I have an interview at a bookshop tomorrow. I'm really nervous.
A little. What questions will they ask me?
Should I wear something special?
Thanks, Uncle Reza. I'll practise my answers in front of the mirror.

speakerB.en: That's normal. Have you read about the shop and its customers?
Probably about your qualifications, your free time and why you want the job.
Wear smart, clean clothes, and arrive ten minutes early to make a good impression.
Good. Speak clearly, smile, and be honest about what you can do.

scenarios.context: A manager interviews a student for a part-time job.

speakerA.en: Thank you for coming, Daniel. Why do you want to work here?
Have you had any work experience before?
We need someone who can work two evenings and every Saturday. Is that possible?
Good. We'll let you know our decision by Friday.

speakerB.en: I enjoy helping people, and I need a job that fits around my studies.
Yes, I helped in my father's shop last summer. I served customers and counted the money.
Yes, that's fine. I finish school at four, so evenings are no problem.
Thank you very much. I would be really happy to join your team.

scenarios.context: A new employee asks a colleague about the job.

speakerA.en: Hi, I'm Mina. It's my first day, and I don't know what to do.
What happens after that?
Is there a break during the shift?
Thanks for being so helpful. I'm less nervous now.

speakerB.en: Welcome! Your shift starts at five. First, put on your uniform and wash your hands.
You'll help the customers and clean the tables. I'll show you how the till works.
Yes, you get twenty minutes. You can eat something in the staff room.
No problem. Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning, so just ask if you're not sure.

scenarios.context: A student asks her manager to change her working hours.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, Mr Karimi. Could I speak to you for a minute?
I have an important exam next Monday. Could I take the evening off?
Yes, my friend Leila said she would work for me. She needs some extra money.
I will. I'm sorry for the short notice, and thank you for being so kind.

speakerB.en: Of course. What's the problem?
I understand. Can you find someone to cover your shift?
In that case, it's fine. Please tell me again on Friday so I can change the plan.
You're a good worker, Mina. Good luck with the exam.
